verified_title: Genie Envisioner: A Unified World Foundation Platform for Robotic Manipulation
problem: Robotic world representation, executable policy learning and action-conditioned evaluation are fragmented; generic video fidelity metrics poorly establish task-relevant physical behavior.
contribution: The paper is the full Genie Envisioner platform, not a standalone paper titled GE-Act: GE-Base supplies multiview sparse-memory video priors, GE-Act adds a160M action decoder, GE-Sim conditions generated video on controls, and EWMBench evaluates robotic video alignment.
algorithm: GE-Base adapts2B LTX-Video/COSMOS2 using three views, sparse historical frames and selected cross-view attention blocks. GE-Act mirrors visual DiT depth with a smaller action branch and cross-attends to cached visual features. Slow-fast mode uses one visual denoising step and five action steps. GE-Sim projects EE pose into pose images plus temporal motion-delta tokens; it is a neural video simulator, not a rigid-body/contact solver.
observations: Language, head and two wrist RGB views, sparse historical frames and optionally robot state. Low-frequency alignment uses5Hz video; action prediction30Hz. New-embodiment adaptation changes learned visual distribution and action head.
actions: GE-Act predicts54-step30Hz chunks. Precise GE-Act control units are insufficiently specified here: introductory prose says torque trajectories, while GE-Sim explicitly conditions on14D bimanual Cartesian pose+gripper. Do not silently equate these representations.
embodiment_and_data: GE-Base pretrains on AgiBot-World-Beta~1M episodes/2967h:7days×32A100 plus3days×32A100 low-frequency alignment. Action pretraining3days×16A100. New Agilex tasks use250demos/~1h PER TASK; DualFranka cloth folding250demos/~1h. Crucially, a NEW action head is trained from scratch for each new embodiment rather than directly reusing AgiBot controls.
experiments: AgiBot five household/industrial tasks compare stepwise SR with end-to-end E2E that allows repeated substep attempts. Stable red-cylinder/cup ablation uses305training demos/40ksteps. Cross-embodiment cloth/box folding and four RoboTwin tasks use supervised adaptation. EWMBench selects10 held-out tasks×100videos, each4–10annotated subactions; trajectory scores choose the best of3 generated samples by reference-distance.
baselines: UniVLA, GR00TN1,pi0 and GO-1 depending on embodiment; matched task-specific data but differing initialization and adaptation. World-video models includeKling,Hailuo,OpenSora,LTX,COSMOS. GE-Sim variants compare LTX/COSMOS, not learned-video versus identified contact physics.

quantitative_result.physical: PDF p12 Table1: GE-Base initialization plus task video adaptation/state gives E2E0.89 and stepwiseSR0.76 versus0.81/0.64 without video adaptation; exact physical evaluation n NOT_EXTRACTED. E2E permits recovery attempts (p11), so it is not per-step first-attempt success.
quantitative_result.latency: PDF p10:54 actions generated in200ms onRTX4090, using one cached visual step/five action steps; not an NX measurement.
quantitative_result.simulation_proxy: PDF p21 Table2:GE-SimPSNR19.9LTX/20.7COSMOS, dynamic score0.78/0.85; these are generated-video metrics, not executed task success. EWMBench best-of3 trajectory selection (p19) is optimistic relative to one deployed prediction.

limitations: Few-shot means250demonstrations/task plus extensive embodied pretraining and retraining the control head. Physical evaluation denominators/confidence intervals are not extracted, and E2E allows retries. EWMBench relies on learned detectors,VLM judgments, references and partial human validation; logical video correctness does not establish force/contact accuracy. Pretraining stays on one robot corpus; parallel-jaw tabletop tasks do not establish whole-body/mobile or dexterous control.
code_and_license: PDF p4 promises code, models and benchmark open-sourcing upon publication. Actual release state, commit and licenses NOT_AUDITED; no execution. A promise is not verified available software.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT sparse real-frame memory and cached-feature compact action heads as separately tested ideas. Existing ACT remains an appropriate comparison. Three camera views,30Hz action conventions and the4090 latency do not match the overview-only Pi station. GE-Sim can provide clearly labeled synthetic visuals for research, but cannot replace Explorer's CAD-based MuJoCo geometry or serve as actual camera/physical-success evidence.
